summary: Rajat Pal works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (MA 2018–2020) and IIT Madras (PhD 2022–2026), where he also held a PhD post.
Rajat Verma works in computational Indology and has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.
Rajeev Kinra is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (1999–2008) and became Associate Professor at Northwestern University in 2007.

Rajeev Kumar works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at M. J. P. Rohilkhand University and Panjab University (PhD 2013), he was a UGC Research Fellow at Panjab University (2013) and Assistant Professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).

Rajeev Sangal specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. Educated at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania, he held faculty posts at IIT Kanpur (1982–1998), IIIT Hyderabad (Professor 2002–2013, 2018–2022), and IIT (BHU) Varanasi (2013–2018).

Rajendra Chandra Hazra was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Sushil Kumar De (~1931–1936). He held posts at Jagannath University (1931), University of Dhaka (1939–1951), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendrakumar Dabee works in philosophy and Indology, holding degrees from the Mauritius Institute of Education, University of Mauritius, Bharathidasan University, Mahatma Gandhi Institute, and University of Madras. He served in the Ministry of Education (1993–2013) and joined MGI as Senior Lecturer in 2013.

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indology and history scholar educated at Hindu School, Calcutta Medical College, and University of Calcutta. He directed Wards' Institution (1856–1881) and served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society.

Rajesh P. N. Rao is a computational Indology scholar who studied at Angelo State University and the University of Rochester under Dana H. Ballard (~1993–1998). In 2000, he became Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University. He later held posts at Presidency University and Scottish Church College.

Raju Rimal works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus, Tribhuvan University, and NMBU (PhD 2015–2019). His posts include the National Archives of Nepal (attested 2018), University of Oslo (2020–2024), and Norwegian School of Sport Sciences (2025).

Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University and University of Calcutta, studying under John Marshall. He worked at the Indian Museum (1910), Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926), and Banaras Hindu University as a professor (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Trijang Rinpoche and Gendun Chopel.

Ralf Kramer is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson. He has served as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and as Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) was a scholar in mathematics and philosophy who studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, Princeton, and UC Santa Cruz (Associate Professor 1968, Professor 1980).
Ralph Lerner is a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1945–1953) under Leo Strauss (~1949–1953). He later held a faculty post at the University of Chicago from around 1959 to 2003.

Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Cambridge under W. H. D. Rouse and E. J. Rapson. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, SOAS (Director 1922–1957), and the Royal Asiatic Society (President 1952–1955).

Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under H. H. Wilson. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1849), Headmaster at Government Sanskrit College (1854), and Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1861–1878).
Ralph Waldo Emerson (1803–1882) was a philosopher and writer who completed his studies at Harvard College, Harvard University (~1817–1821), and Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).

Raluwe Padmasiri is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who became a Professor at the University of Kelaniya in 2012 and is attested as a Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.
